clue.text: Cast off for a change — but where to?

definitions.text: Cast off for a change — but where to?

parts.words: Cast off for a change — but where to?
parts.note: the cast of a play, offstage and needing to swap costumes, go to a particular backstage room

explanation.surface: Someone discarding clothes for a change wonders where to head next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' reads as removing clothes, but the cast are the actors, who go off stage to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors change costume in a backstage room set aside for dressing.

clue.text: Corrupt young lady coming out with a socially acceptable church

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her entrance into society
U means upper-class, socially acceptable in British usage

explanation.surface: A debutante appears in society alongside a respectable church.
explanation.definitionFit: To debauch is to lead into vice, a verb meaning to corrupt morally.

clue.text: Understanding net changes, go in without finishing

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of net are rearranged
without finishing means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Fishing nets are swapped and someone goes in without completing the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' makes ENT from NET; 'without finishing' drops the R of ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Begins increased industrial action?

definitions.meaning: to strike up is to start, as a band starts playing
read literally, more walkouts by workers

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means starts; taken literally it is walkouts on the rise.

clue.text: The main point of Russian Orthodoxy

indicators.note: of says the answer is taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The central idea of Russian Orthodox faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main point' looks like the gist, but it is a cardinal point of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: North is one of the four cardinal compass points, the main directions.

clue.text: Judge America left in denial

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: An American judge left with a denial.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a denial of a request.

clue.text: Exercises in broadcasting out-of-doors

indicators.note: in places the exercises inside broadcasting

parts.note: a programme being broadcast is on air
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Workout routines on TV are filmed outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means outdoors, not under a roof.

clue.text: One aggravates the situation and posts dummy to England (once)

parts.note: jobs are posts or positions
a comforter was the old British name for a baby's dummy, a pacifier

explanation.surface: A trouble-maker sends a fake package to England.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy is the British word for a baby's pacifier; 'comforter' was the older English term.
explanation.definitionFit: Job's friends in the Bible made his suffering worse while claiming to console, so the phrase names an unhelpful consoler.

clue.text: Politicians who can't be said to be worried?

indicators.note: worried in the sense of agitated or shaken up, so the letters of the phrase are tossed about

explanation.surface: Some politicians seem never to be described as anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' reads as anxious, but it is the anagram signal; 'to be' is a link. In British politics the opposition's spokespeople form a team mirroring the government's ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's senior spokespeople are themselves politicians, a group mirroring government ministers.

clue.text: Satellite tribe dressed in gold

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the word for gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: dressed in the sense of prepared or arranged, so the letters of tribe are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribe clad in gold gazes at a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold' is OR, the heraldic tincture; 'dressed' reads as clothed but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiter is a craft or body that circles a planet, which is what a satellite does.

clue.text: Soldiers' brisk jog

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a brisk wind is a fresh one

explanation.surface: Troops set off on a brisk morning run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jog' is not running here: it is a verb, as in jogging someone's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog the memory is to refresh it, a verb meaning prompt or revive.

clue.text: A 9's unusual input into cover for schoolbook

definitions.note: the 's is a link meaning is; 9 refers to the answer at 9-across, a satellite

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the other piece
the cover of a word is its outer pair of letters
unusual signals that the letters of input are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A pupil's odd contribution goes inside the cover of a school exercise book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes PUTNI from INPUT, placed 'into' SK, the outer letters of schoolbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik was the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957.

clue.text: A married man is to make economies

definitions.meaning: to ... resources is to use them sparingly

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a wife's partner; the verb means to manage thriftily.

clue.text: Pigment that's hot in molten core

indicators.note: in says the letter for hot goes inside the recast letters
molten means melted down, so the letters of core are recast

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A pigment containing heat sits within the planet's molten core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'molten' turns CORE into OCRE, with H 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used in paint since prehistoric times.

clue.text: A nasty argument chasing last of buskers from a London street

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the charade comes after that final letter
last of picks out the final letter of the word buskers

parts.note: vile is a synonym of nasty
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A nasty quarrel breaks out among street performers in London.
explanation.walkthrough: SAVILE ROW is a London street famous for bespoke tailoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row is a street in Mayfair, central London, known for its tailors.

clue.text: Revisit — if plastic turns into glass

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: Revisiting something malleable might turn it to glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like a material, but it is the anagram signal on REVISIT and IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitrify is to convert into glass by heat, a verb in the third person here.

clue.text: Where I might grow river grass?

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, an old crossword joke for a river
pot and grass are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A plant wonders whether it could grow river grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river grass' looks like a plant; it is FLOWER (what flows) plus POT. The 'I' is the plant speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant speaking of itself would grow in a container of earth on a windowsill.

clue.text: Old head of English pinching cash machine — a student gets porridge!

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing something between two pieces
head of picks the first letter of English

parts.note: an ATM dispenses cash
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: An old English teacher grabs money from a cash point while a student serves porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like theft; it puts ATM between O and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, cooked as porridge.

clue.text: Green's new leader embracing a bit of mystery

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside
new signals the letters of leader in a new order
a bit of picks out the first letter of mystery

explanation.surface: The Green party's new leader is something of a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Sight first seen in the outskirts of Virginia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: 1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A view first glimpsed on the edges of the state of Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing view, something seen, as a sight is.

clue.text: Name of girl crossing Scottish mountain plant

indicators.note: crossing means stretched across, so the girl's name goes around the mountain

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A girl crosses a Scottish mountain to see a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a flowering garden plant, also called vervain.

clue.text: Manchester, I learn, is somewhat barren

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that Manchester is rather a barren place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means unable to bear offspring or crops, so barren.

clue.text: Withdraw deal given to unprotected crew

indicators.note: unprotected means without its outer covering, so the outer letters of crew are removed

parts.note: to deal with something is to treat it

explanation.surface: A deal is offered to a crew left without protection.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to pull back or withdraw from a position.

clue.text: Giant bird — a nuisance at first

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of nuisance

explanation.surface: A huge bird proves a nuisance from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of enormous size, after the giants of Greek myth.

clue.text: National airlines collapse with no end of competition

indicators.note: a collapse leaves things jumbled, so the letters of airlines are reshuffled
end of picks the final letter of competition, which the rearrangement must lose

explanation.surface: Airlines collapse once there is no competition left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' says the N, the end of competition, is taken from AIRLINES before rearranging AIRLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, so an Israeli is a national of Israel.

clue.text: Smartly turned out worker by the Spanish, say

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
eg, for example, is what say means here
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer standing beside the Spanish looks well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and graceful, as someone smartly dressed is.

clue.text: Invite misery, revealing list

indicators.note: revealing says the answer is shown within the words before it

explanation.surface: Inviting misery is revealed by drawing up a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, as in a list.

clue.text: What to use to calculate climb after slipping?

indicators.note: after places the climbing word behind the slipping word

parts.note: sliding and slipping are synonyms
to scale a wall is to climb it

explanation.surface: Someone works out how to climb again after slipping down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding scale is a rate that moves with another figure, used to work out charges or pay.
